preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and len(s) % 2 == 1 and 1 <= len(s) <= 49 and s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in test_strings)
preconditions.description: Each string s has an odd length between 1 and 49, consisting only of lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(c, str) and len(c) == 1 and c.islower() and c.isalpha() for c in target_chars)
preconditions.description: Each target character c is a single lowercase Latin letter.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly t lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all((c in s and (s.index(c) % 2 == 0) and (s.rindex(c) % 2 == 0)) == (line.strip().lower() == 'yes') for line, s, c in zip(output_lines, test_strings, target_chars))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is 'YES' if and only if the character c appears in s at an even index (0-based) and also at an even index from the end (which is equivalent to checking if the distance from the start to the first occurrence of c is even, and since the total length is odd, the distance from the end to the last occurrence is also even if the first is even). Specifically, since we can delete pairs of adjacent characters, we can reach a specific character c if and only if the number of characters before it is even (so we can delete them in pairs) and the number of characters after it is even (so we can delete them in pairs). Since the total length is odd, if the index of c is even, the number of characters after it is also even. Thus, the condition simplifies to: c must appear in s at an even index.
